name: Waste Isolation Pilot Plant
notes: WIPP is primarily a U.S. Department of Energy transuranic nuclear-waste repository; it hosted the EXO-200 double-beta-decay experiment as a secondary underground physics use. No source fetched in this session gives a founding/opening interval for the facility itself (only for its role as a waste repository), so `intervals` is left empty per v0.2 A17 rather than guessed.

operator_text.quote: Salado Isolation Mining Contractors, LLC. operates the facility for the U.S. Department of Energy
operator_text.value: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Environmental Management (operating contractor: Salado Isolation Mining Contractors, LLC)

depth.note: Converted from the quoted feet figure (2150 ft x 0.3048 = 655.3 m).

summary.plain: An underground salt-bed site in New Mexico built by the U.S. Department of Energy to store nuclear waste. Its deep, quiet tunnels also hosted the EXO-200 physics experiment from 2011 to 2018.
summary.technical: DOE transuranic-waste geologic repository in a salt bed near Carlsbad, New Mexico, with storage rooms ~2150 ft (655 m) underground; hosted the EXO-200 136Xe double-beta-decay detector from 2011 to 2018.
